question: Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) increases by approximately 40–50% during pregnancy, so a serum creatinine of 0.8 mg/dL (70 μmol/L) that would be normal in a non-pregnant woman actually indicates mild renal impairment in the second trimester.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Pregnancy-related GFR increase (40–50%) means that 'normal' creatinine values from standard laboratory reference ranges indicate relative renal impairment in mid-pregnancy. The physiologically expected creatinine is lower — around 0.4–0.6 mg/dL.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! Because GFR rises 40–50% in pregnancy, serum creatinine normally falls to 0.4–0.6 mg/dL (35–55 μmol/L) by the second trimester. A creatinine of 0.8 mg/dL that is 'normal' by standard lab ranges may represent significant renal dysfunction when interpreted in a pregnant woman.
